definition: In machine learning, a ranking SVM is a variant of the support vector machine algorithm, which is used to solve certain ranking problems (via learning to rank).
details: The ranking SVM algorithm was published by Thorsten Joachims in 2002. The original purpose of the algorithm was to improve the performance of an internet search engine. However, it was found that ranking SVM also can be used to solve other problems such as Rank SIFT.

explainer.lead: A variant of the support vector machine used for ranking problems via learning to rank. It matters because it applies SVM-style margin optimisation to ordering results rather than classifying them.

tiers.eli5: Instead of sorting items into yes or no, it learns to put the best items at the top of the list.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it for search result ranking and related ordering tasks; a pitfall is treating it as a plain classifier, when its objective is pairwise ordering and needs ranking-formatted training data.
tiers.paperLevel: A support vector machine variant for ranking problems via learning to rank, published by Thorsten Joachims in 2002; originally aimed at improving internet search engine performance, it also applies to problems such as Rank SIFT.

explainer.example: Train a ranking SVM on query-document pairs labelled by preference to order search results.
